intro: OBJ to STEP converts OBJ files to STEP, the exchange format any CAD program opens, on the server with nothing to install. It is useful, for example, to bring a Blender model into a CAD program to assemble it with other parts.
OBJ is the exchange mesh of Blender, ZBrush, SketchUp and most modelling programs. Here it is converted to STEP.

Each OBJ triangle becomes a flat face of a faceted STEP solid: the CAD program opens, measures and assembles it, but does not recover cylinders or curves, so it cannot be edited as a parametric model. At most 50,000 triangles; if your mesh has more, reduce it first with Reduce polygons.

Each file is converted in an isolated process with bounded memory and time on our server in the European Union, up to five files per task, and deleted when it expires. You can choose the OBJ's units and apply a scale before creating the STEP.

To bring a Blender model into a CAD program to assemble it with other parts, it is worth checking the STEP before using it: open it in your viewer or slicer, check that the parts and their measurements match the OBJ and, if something comes out sideways or too faceted, convert it again with other options. The result note summarises the parts, the triangles and what was done with the OBJ.

faq.q: Can I edit the STEP as if it came from CAD?
faq.a: A STEP made from an IGES or a BREP keeps exact geometry and can be edited; from an OBJ mesh you get a faceted solid.
The colours of the OBJ parts and faces go into the STEP if it is 3MF, OBJ or GLB; STL stores no colours.

faq.q: What happens to the OBJ measurements?
faq.a: OpenCascade turns the OBJ measurements into millimetres in the STEP, which is what slicers and CAD programs expect.
